entries.title: Hermetic Houses Summary
entries.summary: A table of each House with its type, a short description and the benefit it grants at character creation, such as a free Virtue or Mystery.

related.text: ArM5 p.12 The Houses of Hermes

entries.title: The Houses of Hermes
entries.summary: Overview of the twelve Houses and their three kinds: true lineages, which cannot be joined later; Mystery Cults, which are joined by initiation; and societates, which accept magi after training. A magus belongs to only one House at a time.
quotes: It is not possible to join those Houses later.
It is only possible to be a member of one House at a time.

entries.title: The Code of Hermes (overview)
entries.summary: Introduction to the Code of Hermes, the oath sworn by every magus on admission that fixes the Order's structure and limits what its members may do. Enforcement varies, but those caught breaking it usually face their Tribunal.
quotes: all members of the Order recite and swear to it when they are admitted
Magi who violate the Oath and get caught, however, usually find themselves in trouble with their Tribunal.

entries.title: The Code of Hermes (oath text)
entries.summary: The full text of the Hermetic Oath: no depriving or slaying fellow magi except in Wizards' War, abiding by Tribunal votes, not endangering the Order through mundane, demonic or faerie dealings, no scrying on magi, and duties regarding apprentices. Bonisagus magi swear a variant clause.
quotes: I will not deprive nor attempt to deprive any member of the Order of his magical power.
I will have one vote at Tribunal, and I will use it prudently.
I will not use magic to scry upon members of the Order of Hermes, nor shall I use it to peer into their affairs.

entries.title: The Peripheral Code
entries.summary: The body of Tribunal precedent that interprets the Code. Death is the nominal penalty, though Tribunals usually impose fines or service, and refusing a Tribunal's punishment leads to a Wizard's March and Renouncing.
quotes: In theory, the only penalty for breaking the Code is death.
refusing to submit to the punishment imposed by a Tribunal is always taken as reason for the death penalty.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.45

entries.title: Depriving of Magical Power
entries.summary: How the clause forbidding depriving a magus of magical power is applied: Tribunals use it against harm short of physical injury, such as wrecking a lab or killing grogs.
quotes: such as damaging his laboratory or killing grogs.

entries.title: Interfering with Mundanes
entries.summary: How the controversial mundane-interference clause is read: dealings are allowed while they do not harm other magi, but precedent holds that serving as a court wizard breaks the Code.
quotes: As long as dealings with mundanes do not harm other magi, nor seem likely to cause such harm, they are permitted.
Many precedents, however, have established that working as a court wizard is a violation of the Code.

entries.title: Dealing with Demons
entries.summary: The clause against dealing with demons, the one provision the Order enforces absolutely by hunting down offenders.
quotes: This is the only clause enforced absolutely.

entries.title: Molesting the Faeries
entries.summary: How the clause against molesting faeries is interpreted: what counts as molestation is vague and prosecutions turn on politics, but friendly dealings with faeries are not prohibited.
quotes: it does not prohibit friendly dealings with faeries, at any level.

entries.title: Magical Creatures
entries.summary: The Code deliberately gives no protection to magical creatures or other wizards, though excessive interference can still be treated as endangering the Order.
quotes: Notably missing from the Code is a clause granting protection to magical creatures or other wizards.

entries.title: Scrying
entries.summary: How strictly Tribunals read the ban on scrying on magi, with rulings that scrying on a non-magus can count if it reveals a magus's activities, that walking around invisible is scrying, and that Intellego used on an unrecognised magus can be punished.
quotes: simply walking around invisible is magical scrying

entries.title: Apprentices
entries.summary: The apprentice clause is barely enforced, except that the right of Bonisagus magi to take apprentices from other magi and their duty to share work are upheld.
quotes: Magi do not have to train apprentices
The special right of Bonisagus magi to take apprentices from other magi is upheld

entries.title: The Law in Your Saga
entries.summary: Advice to troupes on how strictly the Code is enforced, how strong the Traditionalist and Transitionalist factions are, and how uniform Tribunals are in their saga.

entries.title: Forfeit Immunity
entries.summary: The key defense against Hermetic charges: a magus may lose legal protection in a Wizard War or while committing a crime, and the response must be proportional.
quotes: This lack of legal protection is called forfeit immunity.
While forfeit other magi may act against him, but the response should be proportional.

entries.title: The Hermetic Oath (Interpretation)
entries.summary: Explains that the following sections present a condensed Traditionalist reading of the First Tribunal rulings and that the Presiding Quaesitor is the authority on the Code.
quotes: The Presiding Quaesitor is the authority on the Code

entries.title: High and Low Crimes
entries.summary: Lists the high crimes under the Code and explains that only a high crime allows the prosecution to call for a Wizard's March; all other offenses are low crimes.
quotes: If the case is a high crime, the prosecution can call for a Wizard's March, otherwise he cannot.

entries.title: Deprivation of Magical Power
entries.summary: What counts as depriving a magus of magical power, including injuries, vis, sites, items, familiars, apprentices, books and lab equipment.

entries.title: Slaying a Magus
entries.summary: The prohibition on slaying a member of the Order, the defenses of forfeit immunity and sanctum intrusion, and sample Tribunal rulings.
quotes: being within another's sanctum automatically confers forfeit immunity with respect to the owner of the sanctum

entries.title: Amici
entries.summary: The custom of sworn friendship between magi and the lasting moral duty to avenge an amicus, relevant before declaring a Wizard War.

entries.title: Vagrancy
entries.summary: The legal requirement to belong to a House, the time allowed to find a new one after leaving or being expelled, how sponsorship works, and vagrancy for lacking a residential Tribunal.
quotes: Magi who renounce their House membership or are expelled have one year to obtain membership in another.

entries.title: Endangerment
entries.summary: The Hermetic Oath provision against endangering the Order, what the prosecution must show, and how intent and negligence affect the penalty.
quotes: The prosecution needs to show that magi other than the defendant were endangered.

entries.title: Mundane Interference
entries.summary: The prohibition on interfering in mundane affairs, what it forbids, and how a magus in conflict with a mundane can stay within the law.

entries.title: Deals with Devils
entries.summary: The most strictly enforced high crime: knowingly making an agreement with an infernal agent, the only defense of ignorance, the legality of hunting demons, and a sample ruling.
quotes: Magi are absolutely forbidden from knowingly making an agreement with an infernal agent.

entries.title: Molesting the Fay
entries.summary: What the prosecution must show for a charge of molesting the fay and the defense of reasonable self-protection.
quotes: The prosecution will have to show that a magus or covenant has endangered other magi.

entries.title: Scrying on Members of the Order
entries.summary: What counts as illegal scrying on other magi, the legality of detection magics in a covenant, and the special protection of Redcaps and use of spells without Penetration.
quotes: The key point is 'legal affairs'.

entries.title: Apprentices under the Code
entries.summary: When an apprenticeship legally begins, how an unclaimed Gifted child can be taken, and how adult non-Hermetic wizards join the Order and are sponsored.
quotes: To officially claim an apprentice a magus must initiate them into Hermetic magic.

entries.title: Duty of the Parens
entries.summary: The parens's duty to strike down an apprentice who turns against the Order, who inherits the duty, and the legal consequences of failing to carry it out.
quotes: The Oath demands the parens be the first to attack an outcast magus.

entries.title: Bonisagus Rights and Duties
entries.summary: Oath provisions requiring Bonisagus magi to share their discoveries and Lab Texts and requiring other magi to concede Bonisagus's right to take their apprentices, with a sample ruling.

entries.title: Casting Out
entries.summary: How a convicted magus who refuses the offered lesser punishment is cast out of the Order.
quotes: If taken literally, all convictions should lead to a Wizard's March.

entries.title: Enemies and Allies of the Order
entries.summary: Magi who aid enemies or attack friends and allies of the Order may be prosecuted; only a Tribunal can declare an enemy.
quotes: Only a Tribunal can declare an individual or group as an enemy

entries.title: Interference With the Mundanes
entries.summary: List of activities that in most Tribunals, and especially where Jerbiton magi are active, are not treated as breaking the Code's ban on interfering with mundanes.
quotes: Be identified as a magus, or cast spells before witnesses, provided this doesn't provoke the mundanes.

entries.title: Writing and Responding to Polemic
entries.summary: Introduces the activity of writing persuasive texts in advance of a Tribunal debate, using three forms of writing: polemic, diatribe and apologia.

entries.title: Polemic
entries.summary: A polemic is a summa or tractatus on a knowledge Ability such as Code of Hermes or Order of Hermes Lore that argues for a philosophical position; for these rules a polemic tractatus counts as Level 5.
quotes: tractatus have a Level of 5

entries.title: Diatribe
entries.summary: A diatribe is a critical text written on the same Ability as the polemic it attacks, intended to damage the position and its proponents; each tractatus counts against the author's normal tractatus limit.
quotes: Each tractatus counts towards the normal limit on the number of tractatus that the author may write.

entries.title: Apologia
entries.summary: An apologia is a defensive rebuttal written on the same Ability as the diatribe it answers, strengthening the original proposition; each tractatus counts against the author's normal limit.
quotes: Each tractatus counts towards the normal limit on the number of tractatus that the author may write.

entries.title: Like Father, Like Son (Views from Polemic)
entries.summary: A character who gains their first level in a knowledge Ability by reading a polemic is assumed to share the author's views on that subject.
quotes: any character gaining his first level in a knowledge Ability through reading polemic shares the author's views on that subject

entries.title: The Prevailing Wisdom
entries.summary: The base difficulty of altering opinion in writing depends on how broad the change is; the level is read from the Prevailing Wisdom table.

entries.title: Prevailing Wisdom Table
entries.summary: Table giving the base level of the prevailing wisdom according to whether the change concerns a magus, covenant, Tribunal, House or the whole Order.
quotes: The higher of 3 or the magus' reputation

entries.title: Prevailing Wisdom Examples
entries.summary: Table of sample topics with the Ease Factor that applies to changing opinion about them, and the reason for each.

entries.title: Winning the Argument
entries.summary: Describes how a polemic is written and why it must be of a level high enough to entice readers; its Quality contributes to a bonus in debate at Tribunal.
quotes: Polemical tractatus are treated as level 5 for the purposes of circulating them.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.91 Debate

entries.title: Circulating the Text
entries.summary: A polemic must be circulated through copies, with a seasonal Circulation Roll against an Ease Factor set by the audience; success grants the author a Supporter of (ideal) Reputation.
quotes: Circulation Total: Magus' Reputation + Summa Level (or 5 in the case of tractatus) + Simple Die
Ease Factor: 15 (Tribunal), 18 (House), 24 (the Order)
Each season spent circulating a text provides a bonus of +1 to the next Circulation Total.

entries.title: The Argument Total
entries.summary: Once circulated, the author works out an Argument Total from text quality minus the prevailing wisdom level, which converts into a debate bonus or penalty at Tribunal.
quotes: Argument Total: Text Quality – Prevailing Wisdom Level
the final Argument Total acts as experience points toward buying a debate bonus as per the Art progression table on

entries.title: Responding with Diatribe
entries.summary: A magus who studies a polemic for a season can write and circulate a diatribe whose quality is deducted from the Argument Total, gaining an Opposed to Reputation.
quotes: The diatribe quality is deducted from the current Argument Total

entries.title: Responding with Apologia
entries.summary: Apologia answer diatribes or the original polemic after a season of study and add their quality to the Argument Total; allies other than the original author can write them, and the writer gains a Supporter of Reputation.
quotes: the magus spends a season studying the associated work before writing either summa or tractatus in defense of the original argument

entries.title: Taking the Debate to Tribunal
entries.summary: Describes how the cycle of diatribe and apologia ends in a Tribunal debate, and how bonuses and persuaded parties carry over after a win and are lost after a defeat.
quotes: Where the debate is won, indicated by a positive Argument Strength at the end of the debate, any bonus from circulating the texts also carries over to subsequent Tribunals

entries.title: Correspondences and Other Texts
entries.summary: Debate letters between quarreling magi give a small seasonal study benefit, can serve as supporting testimony in debate, and bundling extra new items with a polemic makes it easier to circulate.
quotes: gains +1 on attempts to circulate the text

entries.title: Winning the Argument Outline
entries.summary: Step-by-step summary of the polemic procedure from defining the argument and writing the text through circulation, apologia and diatribe to the final use of the Argument Total at Tribunal.
quotes: At Tribunal the argument total is used as experience points to buy a bonus (if the total is positive) or a penalty (if the total is negative).

entries.title: Example Polemic, Diatribe, and Apologia
entries.summary: Worked example of writing, circulating and opposing a polemic, showing Quality, circulation totals and the resulting Argument Total and debate bonus.
quotes: The polemic has a Level of 4 and a Quality of 11

entries.title: Determining the Principals
entries.summary: Who becomes prosecution and defense principal in a case, and the order of precedence among volunteers.
quotes: In descending order these are: parens, filius, amicus, covenant sodales and then any other magus.

entries.title: Determining the Tribunal
entries.summary: Rules for deciding which Tribunal hears a case, including border regions, duty to give one's name and residence, and who bears travel costs.
quotes: In all other situations, the case should be brought to the defendant's Tribunal.

entries.title: Publishing a Case
entries.summary: The prosecuting principal must notify the defendant, Presiding Quaesitor and Praeco in advance, usually through Redcaps; later-discovered crimes are heard only if the defendant attends.
quotes: This should be done no later than three months prior to the Tribunal.

entries.title: Lawful Tyranny
entries.summary: A defendant may legally threaten Wizard War to make a prosecutor drop a case; transferring the case to a powerful principal or a Guernicus advocate is the usual counter.
quotes: A prosecuting principal can always transfer a case before publishing it.

entries.title: Transferring a Case
entries.summary: Either principal may hand their case to an advocate; covers the share of fines paid to a prosecution principal and the duty to prepare consistent witness testimony.
quotes: A successful prosecution can net substantial fines, a third of which go to the prosecution principal.

entries.title: Private Hearing
entries.summary: The first stage of presenting a case: both principals summarize in private before the Presiding Quaesitor, who may rule on disputed facts, give an opinion and offer a summary judgment only if both sides agree.
quotes: The Presiding Quaesitor cannot offer a summary judgment unless both the defense and prosecution principal agree to it.

entries.title: Public Hearing
entries.summary: The order of presentation, witness testimony, perjury challenges and voting at a full Tribunal hearing, decided by a simple majority with the Praeco breaking ties.
quotes: A simple majority decides, with the Praeco breaking any ties.

entries.title: Acquittal
entries.summary: After an acquittal the prosecution principal covers the defense principal's costs, and any counter-case begins immediately with roles reversed.
quotes: If a case ends in an acquittal the prosecution principal is liable for all the defense principal's costs.

entries.title: Conviction
entries.summary: After a conviction for a high crime the prosecution may call for a Wizard's March, voted by simple majority with a tie defeating the motion; otherwise the Presiding Quaesitor offers a lesser penalty.
quotes: A simple majority decides, with a tie defeating the motion.

entries.title: Testimony
entries.summary: Rules for giving testimony in person or in writing, perjury challenges and the Presiding Quaesitor's veto of them, Quaesitorial endorsement, and testimony of testimony.
quotes: No magus can be forced to submit to truth-detection spells.

entries.title: Counter-Case Example
entries.summary: Worked example of two magi who each charge the other over a vis source, showing how an acquittal triggers an immediate counter-case.

entries.title: Standard Texts (Roots and Branches of the Arts)
entries.summary: Describes the widely available Roots of the Arts primers and the prized Branches of the Arts summae, which troupes may assign to Arts as needed for their saga.
quotes: These texts vary, but all have a Level of at least 7, and a Quality of at least 21.

entries.title: Acquiring Books
entries.summary: Overview of the Order's book trade: sale of finished books through Redcaps and Tribunals, and scribal hospitality in other covenants' libraries.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.101

entries.title: The Sale of Hermetic Books
entries.summary: Describes the four postal sale methods (public offer, tender, exchange, subscription) and how books are sold at Tribunal.

entries.title: Prices for Books and the Cow and Calf Oath
entries.summary: Introduces the Cow and Calf Oath, a Hibernian ruling restricting resale or gifting of purchased copies, which the later price guidelines assume has been sworn.

entries.title: Mundane Book Prices
entries.summary: Mundane books are bought with cash from a stationer, with a delay of a season for uncommon titles and a cheaper unbound paper version available.

entries.title: Hermetic Book Trade as Barter
entries.summary: Explains that Hermetic books are traded by barter and haggling, and that book values shift with events and with the vis a covenant holds.

entries.title: Least Expensive Books
entries.summary: Guidance on how damaged and discarded books are acquired, typically for about a pawn of vis per damaged summa, with cheap tractatus available in lots after a disaster.
quotes: A covenant wanting to purchase damaged summae with vis can usually find a seller for about a pawn of vis per book

entries.title: Vain Book Prices
entries.summary: Pricing guidance for vain summae and tractatus, and the warning that a vanity book bought from someone other than its author costs as much as a sound one.
quotes: Characters can usually purchase vain summae for half their level in pawns of vis

entries.title: Sound Book Prices
entries.summary: Guideline price in vis for ordering sound summae and tractatus from covenants with permanent copyists, including a surcharge for an immediately available copy.
quotes: These charge a number of pawns of vis equal to the book's level, if the purchaser is willing to wait a season for the copy to be produced.

entries.title: Excellent Books
entries.summary: Books of the highest Quality are normally gifts rather than purchases, with copying restricted; describes how Houses Bonisagus and Tremere handle them.

entries.title: Damages
entries.summary: Damages are paid directly to the victim, including costs of the case, and in a March the victim normally receives a share of the outcast's estate.
quotes: the Presiding Quaesitor will normally grant the victim one quarter of the outcast's estate

entries.title: Fines
entries.summary: How fines are divided between the prosecutor and the Tribunal coffers, and how a March splits the outcast's estate.
quotes: one third is given to the prosecutor, two-thirds to the Tribunal coffers

entries.title: Determining Penalties
entries.summary: How the Presiding Quaesitor sets compensation and punishment, the convicted magus's options (accept, negotiate, refuse), payment deadlines, and appeal to Magvillus.
quotes: If the magus refuses a lesser penalty three times the Quaesitor will declare the magus Marched.
Damages, fines or services should normally be paid or completed in full by the next Tribunal.

entries.title: Punishments (Hierarchy)
entries.summary: Introduces the ladder of Hermetic punishments from seasons of service up to the death of a familiar.
quotes: Punishments are set in a hierarchy to accord with the seriousness of the conviction.

entries.title: Seasons of Service
entries.summary: A convicted magus performs seasons of work for Mercere or Guernicus magi in support of their Tribunal duties, such as longevity rituals, invested devices or copying records.
quotes: The Presiding Quaesitor normally splits the seasons in the favor of Mercere magi.

entries.title: Investing Items (Punishment)
entries.summary: The magus must invest items with negotiated effects and deliver them to Mercere or Guernicus members.

entries.title: Loss of an Apprentice
entries.summary: The convicted magus surrenders their apprentice; the prosecuting principal has first claim and certamen settles competing candidates.
quotes: If multiple suitable candidates step forward, certamen contests decide the matter.

entries.title: Banishment from Tribunal
entries.summary: The magus must avoid the Tribunal's area, arrange others to harvest any vis sources there, and find a new residential Tribunal.
quotes: The magus is required to find another residential Tribunal.

entries.title: Loss of Familiar
entries.summary: The cords binding magus and familiar are cut by a Quaesitorial ritual or a season of lab work, and the former familiar normally cannot be rebound.
quotes: The former familiar cannot normally be rebound.

entries.title: Death of Familiar
entries.summary: The harshest punishment short of a March: the familiar is killed, and some magi choose a March instead.
quotes: The convicted magus's familiar must be killed.

entries.title: Alternatives to Conspiracy
entries.summary: Explains that a magus may harm a mundane rival by helping the rival's enemy without that enemy's knowledge, because conspiracy requires conscious common cause. Examples show acceptable indirect actions.
quotes: Conspiracy requires conspirators working consciously at common cause.

entries.title: Making Riches
entries.summary: Tribunals differ on whether magi may magically make valuable goods, and how doing so lets a covenant lower its peasants' taxes or pay wages and align peasant interests with the covenant.
quotes: Magi can simply produce money magically, but this has created trouble with the mundanes in previous centuries, so making valuable goods is forbidden in some Tribunals.

entries.title: Interference Varies by Tribunal
entries.summary: Contrasts how strictly different Tribunals define interference, from the strict Alps to Normandy, where an action is interference only if it demonstrably harms other magi.
quotes: In Normandy an action is interference if it demonstrably harms the interests of other magi

entries.title: Magic Items
entries.summary: The rules of thumb for selling magic items to nobles: the loophole of selling to mundane servants, typical Tribunal limits on how many items may be sold, and pending political disputes. Story seeds on the topic are included.
quotes: Technically, no magus has been permitted to sell magic items to a nobleman since 1061
The commonest is that a magus may sell at most one magic item to a mortal per year, provided the system of mundane intermediaries is maintained.

entries.title: Involvement
entries.summary: Defines involvement as contact with mundanes that does not breach the Code, and sets the principle that a magus's response must be proportionate to the threat.
quotes: Note that to be acceptable, a magus's actions must usually be proportionate to the threat he faces.

entries.title: Self-Defense
entries.summary: Members of the Order may defend themselves from broadly defined harm, with Tribunal examples of how taxes and land clearing are treated.
quotes: Members of the Order are permitted to defend themselves from harm.

entries.title: Defense of Sodales
entries.summary: Magi may do what any sensible sodalis would ask in that sodalis's defense, such as freeing a captive magus, avenging a harmed Redcap or taking children with the Gift.
quotes: It is not a Hermetic crime to take children with The Gift, even though they are technically not sodales and are often the serfs of lords.

entries.title: Defense of the Art
entries.summary: Magi may treat as an enemy anyone who publicly declares an intent to purge wizards from an area, and may take such a declaration at face value.
quotes: Members of the Order are permitted to treat as an enemy anyone who publicly declares his intent to purge wizards from an area.

entries.title: Demonstrating Harm
entries.summary: Explains that Jerbiton magi and some Mercere covenants intertwine their finances with a city so that damage to its economy counts informally as a Hermetic crime.
quotes: An important part of the process of a plea is the demonstration of harm.

entries.title: Cooperation with Investigations
entries.summary: By Grand Tribunal ruling, magi must cooperate with an official investigation and let their servants be questioned, but need not reveal legal magical secrets.
quotes: Failure to cooperate with an investigation is a low crime.

entries.title: Consultation and Arbitration
entries.summary: Quaesitors may draft and witness agreements or arbitrate disputes; an arbitrated agreement is binding by Grand Tribunal ruling.
quotes: Once agreed, failure to comply with this agreement is an offense by Grand Tribunal ruling.

entries.title: The Presiding Quaesitor
entries.summary: How a Presiding Quaesitor is chosen, the role of his two advisers, his powers of veto and appeal to the Grand Tribunal, and the vote to validate a Tribunal.
quotes: He then calls for a vote to validate the Tribunal, which requires a twothirds majority.

entries.title: Endorsing Testimony
entries.summary: How a Quaesitor magically verifies testimony: the witness lowers all defenses, the Quaesitor checks for manipulation, and conflicting endorsed testimony raises suspicion of infernal involvement.
quotes: the Quaesitor endorsing the testimony must be senior to or at least a peer of the witness

entries.title: The Veto
entries.summary: When a Presiding Quaesitor may veto a ruling, how a veto is reviewed by Magvillus and appealed to the Grand Tribunal, and a suggested troupe roll to judge a clear conflict with the Code.
quotes: This is a very limited judgment, requiring an Int + Code of Hermes roll of 6+ to determine.

entries.title: Wizard's War and the Order
entries.summary: Practical rules of Wizard's War under the Code and Peripheral Code: timing of declaration and duration, limits on harming uninvolved magi, covenant sanctuary, renewed declarations and multiple simultaneous wars.
quotes: A Wizard's War must be declared on the night of a full moon.
It then begins at the rise of the following full moon and lasts until the rise of the third full moon.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.47-48

entries.title: Declaration of War
entries.summary: Optional ways Tribunals may treat service of a Wizard's War declaration when the recipient is absent: forwarding addresses, representatives, Quaesitor review and Redcap delivery.
quotes: Most Tribunals hold a declaration of war to be duly served if the recipient was present at the covenant and the declaration was nailed to the door of his sanctum.

entries.title: Reasons to Declare Wizard's War
entries.summary: Describes the motives and uses of Wizard's War beyond killing, including harassment, committing otherwise illegal acts, vengeance pledges and enforcing pacts.
quotes: The Code permits combatants to kill one another, but it doesn't require them to do so.

entries.title: Preparing for Wizard's War
entries.summary: Advice on defending against Wizard's War: retreating to the covenant and its Aegis, self-imposed exile, personal refuges, and outside assistance such as Moon Duration spells.
quotes: Especially useful are spells of Moon Duration, which last until both the full moon and the new moon have set.

entries.title: Waging Wizard's War
entries.summary: Tactics for fighting a Wizard's War: stealth and reconnaissance, the importance of Arcane Connections to Penetration, finding the enemy, and how magical disguise outpaces detection.
quotes: The real value of an Arcane Connection is the bonus it provides to one's Penetration multiplier (see ArM5, page 84).

entries.title: Certamen
entries.summary: Rules for the formal magical duel: choice of Technique and Form, six totals for initiative, attack, defense, weakening and resistance, Fatigue loss per round, use of vis, and the three ways to win.
quotes: ATTACK TOTAL: Presence + Technique or Form + Stress Die
DEFENSE TOTAL: Perception + Form or Technique + Stress Die
WEAKENING TOTAL: Intelligence + Penetration + Attack Advantage

entries.title: Certamen Example
entries.summary: Worked example of a certamen duel between two magi, from choosing Arts through rounds of attack, defense and Fatigue loss to a concession.
quotes: Moratamis challenged, so she picks the Technique.

entries.title: The Legality of Certamen
entries.summary: Legal limits on Certamen: it cannot be used to defy a Tribunal judgment, force a Code breach or hide a violation, and a mutually accepted challenge cannot be appealed.
quotes: Certamen could not be used to defy a Tribunal judgment, make a magus break the Code or ignore a Code violation.
If a challenge is mutually accepted no Tribunal appeal is possible.

entries.title: Tournament Certamen
entries.summary: Altered certamen rules used at Flambeau tournaments: single elimination, best of three duels per match, rest periods, and who chooses Technique and Form.
quotes: The winner of two out of three duels within the match proceeds to the next round.
The youngest magus chooses the Form, and the oldest the Technique

entries.title: What the Order Remembers (recalling legendary magi)
entries.summary: A simple roll of Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore tells a character how much of a legendary magus's story the Order remembers, graded by Ease Factor tiers from commonly known to lost secrets. House Acclaim or reputation can add bonuses, and some recollections may be false or restricted to a group.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore simple roll and consult the following chart
The character recalls all relevant facts and rumors about that magus up to and including the Ease Factor they achieve.

entries.title: What the Order Remembers of Conciatta
entries.summary: The tiered list of what the Order knows about Conciatta (Known by All through Lost Secrets), with a House Acclaim bonus for Bonisagus characters; some entries are marked as distortions.
quotes: provides Bonisagus characters with a +3 bonus when rolling to remember about her

entries.title: What the Order Remembers of Fortunata
entries.summary: The tiered list of what the Order knows about Fortunata (Known by All through Uncommon Knowledge), with notes that some items are known only to Redcaps or Jerbiton magi and that some legends are false.
quotes: See the Introduction for details on revealing the legend of Fortunata.

entries.title: What the Order Remembers of Hérisson
entries.summary: The tiered list of what the Order knows about Hérisson, with a roll bonus for Bjornaer magi and a larger bonus for members of Clan Arelie.
quotes: receive a +1 bonus to their roll; members of Clan Arelie
receive a +3 bonus instead

entries.title: The Peripheral Code and Case Rulings
entries.summary: Explains that Tribunal rulings together form the Peripheral Code and how earlier case rulings are used by prosecution and defense.
quotes: There are two types of Tribunal ruling, case and proposed.

entries.title: Proposal Rulings
entries.summary: How a magus proposes a new Tribunal ruling, how far in advance it must be published, and how popular rulings spread to other Tribunals.
quotes: Proposals need to be published no later than two years prior to the Tribunal.

entries.title: The Detail of the Peripheral Code
entries.summary: Guidance on inventing Tribunal rulings and a list of the kinds of matters the Peripheral Code normally covers.

entries.title: Magical Silver (Tribunal Ruling)
entries.summary: A Stonehenge Tribunal Peripheral Code ruling that caps the magically created silver a covenant may put into circulation each year, with notes on why gold was not covered and how it affects magi elsewhere.
quotes: No covenant may put more than two pounds of magically created silver per resident into circulation each year.

entries.title: Hermetic Mid-Summer Fair
entries.summary: A gathering hosted by a Greater Alps covenant where magi trade vis, books and enchanted devices, with individual deals or an auction run by the Quaesitores, using barter or vis as currency.
quotes: All exchanges are by barter or by use of vis as currency.

entries.title: Trade and the Order of Hermes
entries.summary: Warns that Hermetic magic gives traders huge advantages and points troupes at the Inflation rules in Covenants when generating vast wealth.
quotes: should familiarize themselves with the Inflation rules given in Covenants, Chapter 5: Wealth & Poverty

entries.title: Creating Wealth Using Magic
entries.summary: List of ways magi can generate profit with magic, from gathering and manufacturing goods to shrinking cargo, magical crews and faster travel.
quotes: Magi are able to create wealth almost effortlessly.

entries.title: Tribunals
entries.summary: What makes a Tribunal legal: attendance requirements, proxy voting with sigils, the presiding Quaesitor, and the Praeco who chairs and controls business. A Tribunal that loses its quorum or presiding Quaesitor ceases to be valid.
quotes: A legal Tribunal must be attended, in person, by at least twelve magi from at least four different covenants.

entries.title: The Grand Tribunal
entries.summary: The Order-wide Tribunal held at Durenmar, attended by delegates from each regional Tribunal and the Primi of all Houses, and the forum for inter-Tribunal disputes.
quotes: The most important Tribunal of the Order is the Grand Tribunal, held every 33 years and drawing magi from the whole Order.

entries.title: Regional Tribunals
entries.summary: How regional Tribunals are formed and run: membership and visiting rules are set locally, Redcaps ensure every magus is invited, and the normal Tribunal rules apply.
quotes: Regional Tribunals meet once every seven years

entries.title: Acquiring House Virtues
entries.summary: How an apprentice gains the free Minor House Virtue: ten seasons of one-to-one interaction with the parens for most Houses, a package for Ex Miscellanea, or an Initiation into the Outer Mystery for Mystery Cult Houses.
quotes: ACQUIRING THE MINOR HERMETIC HOUSE VIRTUE: Requires 10 Seasons of one-to-one Interaction with Parens

entries.title: The End of Apprenticeship
entries.summary: Apprenticeship ends with a gauntlet set by the parens after the usual term; after repeated failures the Quaesitores set the gauntlets.
quotes: If an apprentice fails three gauntlets, the Quaesitores set the fourth and subsequent gauntlets

entries.title: Body Modification Rules
entries.summary: Introduces the body modification techniques that magi of many Houses know and Criamon magi use on themselves and apprentices.

entries.title: Tattoos
entries.summary: Distinguishes Criamon stigmata from ordinary ink tattoos, which can carry magic, and explains the social reaction to tattoos including the Disfigured Flaw for a visible tattoo.
quotes: A single visible tattoo is sufficient to earn the Disfigured flaw

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition (Inscription on the Soul)

entries.title: Charters
entries.summary: Explains what a charter is and how it is structured, and why magi who engage with the mundane world will increasingly record rights and obligations in charters with nobles.

entries.title: Optional Rule: Charter Strength
entries.summary: Optional rule giving each side of a charter a strength score generated by notaries, which is then tested by a seasonal search for loopholes that justify breaking provisions.
quotes: Charter Strength: Intelligence + Civil and Canon Law + Stress Die
There is a default of three botch dice for this roll

entries.title: Case Rulings (Debate at Tribunal)
entries.summary: How a contested Tribunal case is debated, including the use of testimonies to boost Attack or Defense Totals once each, with a table of bonuses by type of testimony.
quotes: Each testimony possessed by an opponent may be used once per debate to support an argument.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, House Guernicus

entries.title: Proposal Cases (Debate at Tribunal)
entries.summary: How a magus proposing a clarification, addition or alteration to the Code is debated against the whole Tribunal, with a table of penalties to Argument Strength by type of case.
quotes: Once all the points have been debated, the proposer's Argument Strength is used to determine the margin of victory in the usual way.

entries.title: Dimicatio
entries.summary: Tournament contest in which magi cast real spells at each other using forceless casting while defending with fast-cast defenses; the first spell to reach the opponent's Parma wins.
quotes: The first magus whose spell reaches his opponent's Parma is the winner.

entries.title: Dimicatio in Detail
entries.summary: How to play out a dimicatio with the normal combat rules: range, initiative, alternating offensive spells and fast-cast defenses judged by the storyguide.
quotes: Both competitors roll Initiative and the winner casts the first offensive spell.
a fast-cast defense of one-half the level of the incoming spell is usually sufficient

entries.title: Apprenticeship's End: The Gauntlet
entries.summary: The Gauntlet is the parens' test that decides whether an apprentice becomes a magus; it covers who sets it, how long a parens may delay it, how to run it as an adventure, and an optional single roll to pass it.
quotes: Make an Intelligence + Ability + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 9 for the apprentice character.
OPTIONAL RULE FOR PASSING A GAUNTLET: Apprentice's Intelligence + Appropriate Ability + stress die vs. 9

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.83 Tytalus

entries.title: Houses of Hermes Gauntlets
entries.summary: Sidebar summarizing the typical Gauntlet of each Hermetic House and how to build a pre-Gauntlet adventure around it.
quotes: An apprentice of House Tremere must face his master in certamen to pass his Gauntlet.

entries.title: Obligations and the Code of Hermes
entries.summary: Explains how heavy covenant obligations interact with the Oath of Hermes ban on depriving a magus of magical power, and why a covenant may not change obligations against a magus's will.
quotes: the covenant cannot alter the obligation imposed on any magus against his will without committing a High Crime

entries.title: The Official Seal (Quaesitorial Ratification of a Charter)
entries.summary: Some Tribunals require a charter to be approved by the Quaesitores, who may add it to the Peripheral Code; a Quaesitor can only demand changes where the charter breaks the Oath of Hermes or the Peripheral Code.
quotes: No Quaesitor can dictate the contents of a charter

entries.title: Nobility
entries.summary: How nobles interact with covenants and what the Peripheral Code allows: deals not involving service or permanent magical aid are generally not interference with mundanes, though killing a noble rival invites a Wizard's March.
quotes: The Peripheral Code has tended to rule that deals with nobles that don't involve service or permanent magical aid are not a violation of the clause against interfering with mundanes.

entries.title: Other Wizards
entries.summary: The Order's 'join or die' policy toward non-Hermetic wizards, rarely enforced, except that any non-Hermetic wizard who learns Parma Magica or similar general magic resistance must join or be hunted down.
quotes: Any non-Hermetic wizard who learns the Parma Magica, or any other form of general magic resistance, must join the Order of Hermes or be hunted down.

entries.title: The Sanctum
entries.summary: Any magus may declare a sanctum, within which an intruding magus has no legal protection; the Grand Tribunal ruling prescribes how the sanctum is marked.
quotes: A decision of the First Tribunal means that a magus in another's sanctum has no legal protection from the owner of the sanctum

entries.title: Sanctum and the Code
entries.summary: The Code of Hermes lets each magus claim one marked sanctum where trespassers may be slain without penalty.
quotes: The owner may slay a magus trespassing in a sanctum without penalty.
A magus may have only one sanctum at a time

entries.title: Tribunals and the First Tribunal
entries.summary: Distinguishes the First Tribunal from the regional and Grand Tribunals, which matters for the hierarchy of Tribunal rulings.

entries.title: Abide by Tribunal Decisions
entries.summary: Whose rulings bind whom: regional Tribunal rulings apply to residents and visitors, First and Grand Tribunal rulings apply everywhere, and regional rulings may not contradict higher ones.
quotes: A regional Tribunal cannot rule in contradiction to First and Grand Tribunal rulings.

entries.title: Proxy Voting
entries.summary: How a magus can give his sigil to another magus to vote for him at Tribunal, the difference between directed and free proxies, the obligation to report the vote, and the Tremere practice of holding filii's sigils.
quotes: A magus can give his sigil to an attending magus who agrees to act as proxy.
Not following the instructions is a high crime.

entries.title: Voting Rights and Residency
entries.summary: Each magus's single vote at their residential and the Grand Tribunal, how residency is chosen and changed, delinquent residency, and the duty to vote prudently.
quotes: Each magus must have a single Tribunal of residence.
Such a magus has seven years to meet the requirements or join another Tribunal.

entries.title: Wizard War
entries.summary: The legal procedure and limits of a Wizard War: delivery of the declaration, the time to prepare and the duration, what property may be attacked, immunity from prosecution, and sample rulings.
quotes: the recipient of the declaration has a lunar month to prepare and then the war lasts for a lunar month
A magus cannot legally attack property in which his opponent has shared ownership, such as covenant buildings, vis sites and covenant books.

entries.title: Military Service and Wizard War
entries.summary: Discusses how military service owed under charters can be met by sending men or paying scutage rather than fighting in person, and gives the core interpretation that Wizard War needs a month's notice, which each Tribunal may rule on.
quotes: notice of a lunar month must be provided before hostilities commence

entries.title: Legal Issues for Apprentices
entries.summary: Covers the Code of Hermes provisions on apprentices: legal recognition on Opening the Arts, the season of instruction, the apprentice as the parens' property in Wizards' Wars and trades, the parens' liability, no appeal for the apprentice, and fosterage.
quotes: The parens must personally instruct the apprentice for one season during each year of apprenticeship

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.17

entries.title: Hermetic Disguises and Personae
entries.summary: Notes on how the Code of Hermes treats magi who keep a disguise in another covenant or impersonate Quaesitores and Redcaps, including that magical impersonation can be prosecuted as scrying.
quotes: This magus was successfully prosecuted for scrying, because he used magic to take the appearance of the Redcap

entries.title: Failing an Apprentice
entries.summary: Apprentices fail mainly by losing The Gift, gaining the Failed Apprentice Social Status in place of Apprentice, or by being abandoned by their parens, which is a low crime and leaves the apprentice outside the Order.
quotes: Once The Gift is lost, the character immediately gains the Minor Social Status Virtue: Failed Apprentice

related.text: Guardians of the Forests p.114 Fenistal

entries.title: Acquiring House Virtues
entries.summary: An apprentice gains the free Minor House Virtue after enough seasons of one-on-one interaction with the parens, while Mystery Cult Houses use an initiation into the Outer Mystery and House Ex Miscellanea gives a package of Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: ACQUIRING THE MINOR HERMETIC HOUSE VIRTUE REQUIRES 10 SEASONS OF ONE-ON-ONE INTERACTION WITH PARENS

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.16 Ritual of Twelve Years

entries.title: Second Laboratories
entries.summary: Sidebar on why few magi keep a second lab, noting that the Peripheral Code allows only one sanctum and that a lab must occupy a single chamber.
quotes: the Peripheral Code only allows a magus to maintain one sanctum

entries.title: The Nature of the Plea
entries.summary: How noblemen make a legal complaint against the Order in different Tribunals, who administers the facilities, and how mundane society regards such pleas as having no real authority.
quotes: Most Tribunals have some way for noblemen to make known that they have a legal issue with the Order.

entries.title: Delaying Opening the Arts
entries.summary: A magus may delay Opening the Arts, but the child is not legally his apprentice until then and other magi may take her; keeping a Gifted lab assistant is a low crime.
quotes: He can declare the child his apprentice, but she isn't legally bound to him until he Opens her Arts.

entries.title: Letters of Authority and Allies of Quaesitors
entries.summary: Non-Quaesitors can investigate on a Quaesitor's behalf if given a letter of authority, which grants investigation immunity and the right to demand cooperation; authority can be granted retroactively for successful investigations.
quotes: authority can be given retroactively, and normally is for successful investigations

entries.title: Saga Background: The Order of Hermes
entries.summary: The troupe decides how organized and intrusive the Order is in practice, from strict registration and enforcement to loose social Tribunals, which changes how much politics the saga contains.
quotes: How organized is the Order in practice?

entries.title: Sanctum Law (Marked Texts)
entries.summary: Grand Tribunal rulings let magi protect texts with a sanctum mark, even outside the sanctum, and let a House symbol mark a text as secret to the House. Reading such a marked text is a low crime for other magi.
quotes: A magus who reads from such a marked text is committing a low crime.

entries.title: Magical Items
entries.summary: The 1061 rulings that bar taking mundane payment for arcane services from anyone outside the Order, and the two loopholes: payment in arcane items or vis, and mundane covenant members reselling items or taking commissions.
quotes: making it illegal to accept money or other mundane goods as payment for arcane services from anyone other than a member of the Order of Hermes or a Hermetic covenant

entries.title: Tournament Prizes
entries.summary: Guidance on the kinds of prizes a tournament host offers, with vis as the simplest.
quotes: a rook (ten pawns) is a moderate prize

entries.title: Wizard's March
entries.summary: What it means to be cast out of the Order: outlaw status, the parens's duty, the sanctity of Tribunal grounds and the usual grace period before the outcast can be attacked.
quotes: Normally, magi that the Tribunal has voted to cast out have until the end of the Tribunal before they can be legally attacked.

entries.title: Wizards' War
entries.summary: The procedure by which a feud between two magi becomes a formally declared open war in which they may kill each other without breaking the Code, timed by the moon. Overuse risks a Wizard's March.
quotes: The war then begins on the rise of the following full moon, and lasts until the rise of the next full moon after that.

entries.title: Wizards' Melee
entries.summary: A tournament team event where a magus and grogs try to touch the opposing magus with a forceless spell; lists the usual restrictions on ranges, weapons, damage spells and devices.
quotes: Each team consists of one magus and five grogs.
blunted weapons (–3 to Damage)

entries.title: Bjornaer: The Heartbeast
entries.requires: House Bjornaer: Initiation into the Heartbeast mystery
entries.summary: Bjornaer magi take the form of one mundane creature using the Heartbeast Ability; the form cannot be changed by Hermetic magic, they can cast in beast form at a penalty, cannot bind familiars, and gain little Warping from changing.
quotes: In that case, a roll of Stamina + Heartbeast against an Ease Factor set by the storyguide allows the character to change anyway.
As a rule of thumb, 3 + the magnitude of the transforming magic is a reasonable number.

entries.title: The Heartbeast (concept and Ritual of Twelve Years)
entries.requires: Virtue: Heartbeast (Ritual of Twelve Years, House Bjornaer)
entries.summary: Explains what the heartbeast is, that only the Ritual of Twelve Years grants the Heartbeast Virtue and Ability, and how it differs from magical shapechanging (a true animal, not a disguise). Also covers pregnancy, cross-species children and the House's bond of kinship.
quotes: Undergoing the Ritual of Twelve Years is the only way to gain the Heartbeast Virtue (and Ability)

related.text: ArM5 pp.91-92 Outer Mystery of House Bjornaer

entries.title: Choosing the Heartbeast
entries.summary: Advice for players on choosing a heartbeast that fits the character: expect physical signs, think about other Bjornaer in the troupe, and remember a magus can have only one.
quotes: Naturally, a magus can only have one heartbeast, for he only has a single spirit.

entries.title: Heartbeast Temperaments and Restrictions
entries.summary: Sorts heartbeasts into four temperaments, pure or aspected by another, and lists which creatures cannot be heartbeasts (domesticated animals, creatures with Might, those outside the Size limits). Includes the Size option for very small heartbeasts.
quotes: Creatures Smaller than a Weasel (Size –7)
Creatures Larger than an Aurochs (Size +3)

entries.title: Example Heartbeasts
entries.summary: Sidebar table assigning example animals to each heartbeast temperament and aspect.

entries.title: Plant Heartbeasts
entries.summary: Optional rule allowing an unusual plant 'heartbeast': the plant form can do only what a plant can do, and the character is likely to have Cyclic Magic.

entries.title: Changing Form (heartbeast)
entries.summary: A Bjornaer magus assumes his heartbeast form in a round, usually without a roll. A Stamina + Heartbeast roll is needed to overcome a shapechanging or magic-suppressing spell, and the animal form cannot cast.
quotes: making a Stamina + Heartbeast roll, against an Ease Factor of (3 + magnitude of the spell)

entries.title: The Hidden Shape
entries.summary: Explains that, because of the Limit of Essential Nature, the heartbeast form appears to Hermetic magic as a mundane animal and has no ongoing effect after the transformation, though active magic on the magus can still be detected.

entries.title: Bjornaer Magi and Familiars
entries.summary: Initiation into the Heartbeast mystery makes it impossible to bind a familiar, and a magus who has ever bound one cannot complete the ritual.
quotes: Any magus who has ever bound a familiar, even if it has since died, cannot successfully complete the Ritual of Twelve Years

entries.title: Heartbeasts and Wizard's Twilight
entries.summary: What happens when a Bjornaer magus enters Twilight. Wizard's Twilight usually brings the heartbeast form, and Final Twilight yields a mundane beast or, with an Inner Mystery, a Great Beast with a Magic Might derived from the Heartbeast Ability.
quotes: acquires a Magic Might equal to (5 x Heartbeast Ability)

entries.title: Heartbeast (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: The Heartbeast Ability gives knowledge of the animal form, a Personality Trait named for the animal, and the power to change form. It cannot be learned from books and can only be taught by someone with the same temperament.
quotes: at a level equal to half the score in this Ability

entries.title: Path of Seeming
entries.summary: Introduces the Path of Seeming, which looks for weak points in time by examining the world's distracting details.

entries.title: Station of Differentiation of Seeming
entries.summary: First station of the Path of Seeming: the magus gains Clear Thinker, Common Sense and Keen Vision (or a similar sense Virtue) after a gruel-and-water investiture.
quotes: Each magus develops the Clear Thinker, Common Sense, and Keen Vision Virtues

entries.title: Station of True Sight
entries.summary: Second station: after a season of mad wanderings the magus can use Enigmatic Wisdom as both Second Sight and Magic Sensitivity and gains the Vow Flaw.
quotes: They may use their Enigmatic Wisdom score as if it were both the Second Sight and Magic Sensitivity Abilities.

entries.title: Station of Vivid Memories from Objects
entries.summary: The magus can recall an object's history by handling it, rolling Perception + Enigmatic Wisdom against Ease Factors based on how often the detail occurred, with a bonus for vivid events.
quotes: A magus seeking a particular memory makes a Perception + Enigmatic Wisdom roll.
Add +3 to the Perception + Enigmatic Wisdom roll for vivid events.

entries.title: Station of Passing Through Seeming
entries.summary: The magus sends his spirit travelling as a ghostly form that can see and speak at the destination and cast limited spells, while his body lies as if dead.
quotes: At their destination, they may cast spells at Arcane Connection range.

entries.title: Passing Through Rules
entries.summary: Spirit-travel total and the totals needed to reach familiar, previously visited, unknown and distant places.
quotes: A magus's Pass Through Seeming Total is a simple die + Intelligence + Enigmatic Wisdom + the magical aura of his destination.
hindered by an Aegis of the Hearth as if they were creatures with a Magic Might score of five times their Enigmatic Wisdom

entries.title: Station from Which to Ignore the Real
entries.summary: The magus can briefly treat solid mundane objects as spectral with a Stamina + Concentration roll, with the Ease Factor rising for more objects; the station also makes Twilight more likely.
quotes: With a Stamina + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of six, and a round of preparation
The Ease Factor increases by one for every object after the first.

entries.title: Path of Strife
entries.summary: Introduces the Path of Strife, the House's worldly and morally transgressive path whose followers do sinful work on behalf of the House and hunt demons.

entries.title: Station of the Eater of Sin
entries.summary: First station: the magus senses strife, uses Enigmatic Wisdom as Magic Sensitivity without reducing Magic Resistance, gains the Blatant Gift, and uses Enigmatic Wisdom as a score for one weapon type.
quotes: They may use their Enigmatic Wisdom as the Magic Sensitivity Ability, but they do not subtract it from their Magic Resistance.
A magus on this path may use his Enigmatic Wisdom score as if it were a score for a single type of weapon.

entries.title: Station of Blood and Bronze
entries.summary: Meditation can rot or rust objects and kill mundane things in an area, and weapon strikes gain greatly increased Attack and Penetration; the magus can no longer enter Final Twilight.
quotes: They have four times the usual Attack Total, and can injure creatures immune to non-magical attacks.
This power's Penetration is (magus's Enigmatic Wisdom x 5), taking the Form of the weapon's striking edge.
which can be no wider than 500 feet across per level of Enigmatic Wisdom that the magus possesses

entries.title: Station That Repels and Attracts Elements
entries.summary: The magus can attract or repel objects of a single Form at will, limited by combined weight, with no Penetration and no effect on warded objects.
quotes: provided their combined weight does not exceed the magus's weight multiplied by three

entries.title: Station That Charms the Elements
entries.summary: The magus can talk to elementally pure objects and persuade their spirits to give information or move, using Presence + Charm rolls against Ease Factors set by the request.
quotes: With a Presence + Charm roll against an Ease Factor of 9 a magus can convince a spirit to give information, or to move in minor, useful ways.

entries.title: Station of Golden Cider
entries.summary: The magus strips supernatural properties from items, creatures and some Gifts by touch after a preparatory meditation, at the cost of losing Creo with most Forms.
quotes: the magus must have an Enigmatic Wisdom score at least one-fifth of the victim's Magic Resistance
this power has a Penetration score of (Enigmatic Wisdom x 5), with a Form of Corpus

entries.title: Repose on the Path of Strife
entries.summary: Followers of this path cannot enter Final Twilight and instead die creating adulterations, so many end their lives by using Golden Cider on themselves.

entries.title: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: Introduces the Path of Walking Backwards and lets followers choose a reasoned labyrinth walk or an ecstatic dance; dancers use Dexterity for Enigmatic Wisdom rolls during labyrinth meditations.
quotes: Spinners and dancers use Dexterity rather than Intelligence when making Enigmatic Wisdom rolls during Labyrinth meditations

entries.title: Station of Service to Harmony
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: First station: after purification under a Mystagogue the magus's Gift becomes Gentle, or a Blatant Gift is removed.
quotes: The Gift of most characters on this path becomes Gentle.

entries.title: Station of Rice and Honey
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: By labyrinth meditation the magus restores damaged objects to wholeness and can hold a dying person on the threshold of death for a limited time, but gains the Noncombatant Flaw.
quotes: This power has a Penetration score of the magus's Enigmatic Wisdom multiplied by five.
A magus may safely continue performing meditations for a number of hours equal to his Enigmatic Wisdom score.

entries.title: Station of Expression
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: The magus gains Free Expression and Inspirational, may use Enigmatic Wisdom as an artistic skill, and can convey complex ideas through artworks to mundane audiences.
quotes: Each magus who completes this avenue gains the Virtues Free Expression and Inspirational, and may use Enigmatic Wisdom in lieu of one artistic skill

entries.title: Station of Exaltation
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: By labyrinth meditation the magus draws out a latent positive property from a mundane object, with a difficult roll needed to know which will appear; the magus loses Perdo with most Forms.
quotes: an extremely difficult Intelligence + Enigmatic Wisdom roll (Ease Factor 21 or more)

entries.title: Threshold of Repose on the Path of Walking Backwards
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: The final station lets the magus freely change age, gender and species and choose the time of death, or ascend to join the Spharios.
quotes: A magus of this station may select his age, gender, and species as often as he wishes, taking only the time of a breath to change.

entries.title: Twilight and Walking Backwards
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of Walking Backwards
entries.summary: The threshold of repose gives no Twilight immunity, though abstaining from magic and strong supernatural auras and avoiding multiple Warping Points at once avoids Twilight.
quotes: magi who abstain from all use of magic and stay out of powerful supernatural auras can avoid entering Twilight by avoiding gaining two or more Warping Points at once

entries.title: Clan Arelie (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Remember clan, its political stance and roles, and lists its three Clan Initiations (the Trial of the Tree, the Deed of Forgotten Lore and the Oath of the Empty Hand) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The initiate is hanged by his wrists for four days

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 3: Curious Common Magics (Art of Memory)

entries.title: Clan Ilfetu (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Teach clan, the only one that initiates the House Mysteries, and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial and Oath of the Prophet and the Deed of Honor) with the Virtues and Flaws gained.
quotes: To be a member of this clan, you must take the Clan Ilfetu Minor Virtue.
The Initiate is pinned under a large rock for 9 days and acquires the Visions Flaw

entries.title: Clan Maruhs (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Strive clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Chains, the Deed of Emulation and the Oath of the Muse) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: Bound by magical chains and cast into a pit

entries.title: Clan Midusulf (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Lead clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of the Sacred Marriage, the Deed of Glory and the Oath of Steadfastness) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate is ritually wedded to the earth through the letting of blood

entries.title: Clan Sirnas (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Protect clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Self Control, the Deed of the Woodland Warden and the Oath of the Helpful Stranger) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate must starve himself until he collapses

entries.title: Clan Wilkis (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Nourish clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Self-Negation, the Deed of Fealty and the Oath of Completion) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate must perform humiliating and degrading acts before many witnesses

entries.title: Enigmatic Wisdom for Magi From Other Houses
entries.requires: House Criamon (or a magus of another House studying with it)
entries.summary: Sidebar allowing an outsider to study a year with a Criamon magus or ghost and gain the Enigmatic Wisdom Ability at a score of 1, which may lead to an offer of membership.
quotes: gain the Enigmatic Wisdom Ability, with a score of one

entries.title: Riddles (Criamon apprenticeship and Enigmatic Wisdom)
entries.summary: Explains how each Criamon apprentice receives fifteen riddles to ponder, which builds the Enigmatic Wisdom mindset, the Riddle of the Magus that replaces the Gauntlet, and how apprentices choose a path.
quotes: At the beginning of her apprenticeship, each Criamon apprentice is given fifteen riddles

entries.title: Rolls for Riddles
entries.summary: Optional Ability roll for composing or answering riddles instead of roleplaying them, when a magus receives a new riddle, and how accumulated answers slowly lower the Ease Factor.
quotes: They roll Intelligence + Enigmatic Wisdom, against an Ease Factor that varies between three and 25

entries.title: Enigmatic Wisdom for Criamon
entries.summary: Overview of Enigmatic Wisdom as the start of every path, trained by meditating on riddles and deepened by the insights of others.

entries.title: Symbolic Understanding
entries.summary: Criamon use Enigmatic Wisdom to read stigmata, detect Warping and interpret dreams and visions, with Ease Factors for how much they learn.
quotes: a successful Intelligence + Enigmatic Wisdom roll against an Ease Factor of 6
Perception + Enigmatic Wisdom roll against an Ease Factor six or more

entries.title: Labyrinth Meditations
entries.summary: A walking meditation in a labyrinth grants a bonus to one roll for an hour, with the meditation time and need for a physical maze shrinking as Enigmatic Wisdom rises.
quotes: The bonus is equal to half the magus's Enigmatic Wisdom score.
Labyrinth rituals take sixteen hours for characters with a score of one in Enigmatic Wisdom.

entries.title: Promotion by Force
entries.summary: Introduces the alternative promotion path in House Tremere: instead of being promoted politically, a magus may claim a rank by dueling, with the dishonor of using vis against other Tremere in such duels.
quotes: When dueling with other Tremere magi, it is dishonorable to use vis.

entries.title: Claiming the Name (Gauntlet by Certamen)
entries.summary: Explains the Tremere Gauntlet as a certamen challenge from apprentice to master for the title of magus, how it is staged and judged, and the ceremony of the birchwood wand that serves as the new magus's sigil.
quotes: It is all-but unheard of for an apprentice to win the role of magus by force

entries.title: Claiming the Sigil (Experienced Magus by Force)
entries.summary: How a Tremere magus challenges his parens for his own sigil (once at a chosen time, then at each Decennial), and the privileges of a young magus who holds his own sigil, including how aid is treated and trivial votes at Tribunal.
quotes: The protégé may challenge for their sigil, at a time of their choosing, once.
After this, the magus may challenge at every Decennial meeting of the House.

entries.title: Claiming the Tribunal's Dragon Banner (Exarch by Force)
entries.summary: How an exarch's heir is chosen by dueling and how any Tremere magus may challenge an exarch to certamen once, with restrictions on timing and the Primus's possible responses; includes the Addled Secutor story seed.
quotes: A magus may only challenge the exarch for his role once, and must not do so while the House faces rivals, at Tribunal for example.

entries.title: Dissent (House Tremere)
entries.summary: Describes how the House handles periods of dissent, the mechanisms for healing rifts, and how dissent reduces the support available to player characters from different parts of the House.
quotes: In a time of dissent, most members of the House pretend that the structure is still functioning normally.

entries.title: Claiming the Sigil of Tremere (Primus by Force)
entries.summary: The process by which a Primus is replaced: succession by the legatus on retirement or death, and the Decennial duels among councilors to name a secutor who may challenge the Primus, with limits on repeated challenges.
quotes: The secutor may challenge the Primus as often as he wishes.

entries.title: Beloved Rivals (Tytalan Formal Rivalry)
entries.summary: Describes the Tytalan custom of formally declaring a lifelong rivalry, how it is declared and what it commits the rivals to, and the formal modes of address that tell other Tytali not to interfere.
quotes: Beloved Rivals most commonly exist between master and pupil, but could potentially exist between any pair of Tytali who have sufficient cause.

entries.title: Eristic Moots
entries.summary: Explains the eristic moot, a public dispute between Tytalan magi: who may attend, how the permitted weapons (debate, combat, certamen, magic) are agreed in advance, and the two special moots, the Apprentice's Gauntlet and the choice of a new Primus.
quotes: By convention, the minimum attendance for an eristic moot is five

entries.title: Tytalan Apprenticeship
entries.summary: Describes how House Tytalus trains apprentices, from the education before opening the Arts through the harsh years of training and the Book of Instruction, and what happens to apprentices who fail to react to it.
quotes: During the next 15 years, the apprentice's life is exceptionally hard.

entries.title: The Apprentice's Gauntlet
entries.summary: How a Tytalan apprenticeship ends: the apprentice must force his master to accept him as a magus in an eristic moot, with consequences (Self Confident, Weak Parens, Tormenting Master) depending on how and when the Gauntlet is passed.
quotes: The apprentice passes his Gauntlet if he can make his master accept him as an equal.
An apprentice who succeeds in killing his master at any point in his apprenticeship is elevated to the status of magus immediately, regardless of the state of his training.

entries.title: Joining House Tytalus
entries.summary: Explains how a magus of another House or a hedge wizard can become Tytalus by forcing a Tytalan magus to accept him, that dual membership is allowed only here, and how a magus leaves the House.
quotes: Of course, since House Tytalus is the only one of the 12 Houses that permit dual membership

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, House Guernicus

entries.title: Tytalan Cabals
entries.summary: Describes how Tytalan cabals are formed and run: anonymous invitations, disguised attendance, an inaugural meeting, consensus tasking and closed membership.
quotes: A cabal is usually initiated by a single magus, who decides that he needs support in completing a specific goal.

entries.title: Societas Merceris: Followers of Belin
entries.requires: Redcap society: Followers of Belin (Legacy flaw)
entries.summary: A Redcap society of elite messengers descended from or adopted into Belin's line, with character requirements limiting them to humble, diligent Personality traits and the Legacy flaw.
quotes: they must take the Legacy flaw (see the Appendix, Virtues and Flaws)

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Pawnbrokers
entries.summary: A Redcap society that stores vis in distinctively shaped tokens; members may trade starting magic item levels for vis in their signature shape and receive a yearly pawn of vis from the House.
quotes: Pawnbroker Redcaps may trade two levels of their starting magic items for a pawn of vis in their signature shape

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Bloodcaps
entries.requires: Redcap society: Bloodcaps (Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood, plus a Malediction)
entries.summary: A Redcap society of faerie-blooded border guards; members must take Faerie Blood and a Greater or Lesser Malediction triggered by the cross or scripture, and tend to carry combat-oriented magic items.
quotes: All Bloodcaps must take Faerie Blood (or Strong Faerie Blood)

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Goliards
entries.requires: Redcap society: Goliards (Clerk or Educated, plus a Compulsion)
entries.summary: An artistic, hedonistic Redcap society; members must take Clerk or Educated and a Compulsion toward an inspirational vice, and commonly take Free Expression, Inspirational or a Hermetic Patron.
quotes: characters must take either Clerk or Educated

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Cult of Heroes
entries.requires: Redcap society: Cult of Heroes (Blood of Heroes for hero characters; Mythic Blood or Mercurian Magic and Pagan for magi)
entries.summary: A society that raises exceptional children as heroes; hero characters take the Blood of Heroes virtue, may trade starting magic item levels for Characteristic increases, and Cult magi may substitute Mastered Spells for Puissant Art.
quotes: Either type may exchange 10 levels of effects in their starting magic items for a +1 increase to any of their negative Characteristics.

entries.title: Societas Merceris: Milvi Antiquiti
entries.requires: Redcap society: Milvi Antiquiti (Mutantum Magic for magi)
entries.summary: A Mutantes society that copies and lends ancient books to magi for a vis fee and carries them by shapeshifting into birds; magi members take Mutantum Magic and Redcap members usually learn Latin, Scribe and Magic Theory.
quotes: usually 1p a season or 3p a year

entries.title: Path of the Body
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of the Body
entries.summary: Introduces the Path of the Body, its five stations and the alternative order of the second and third stations, which changes the scripts and when the Pious Flaw is gained.
quotes: a Major Flaw (Pious) is always gained in the third avenue

entries.title: Station of the Perfect Tool
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of the Body
entries.summary: First station of the Path of the Body: a Corpus aspect with Minor Potency, Enigmatic Wisdom substituted for healing Abilities, and the Vow and Deleterious Circumstances Flaws.
quotes: They may use Enigmatic Wisdom in place of Chirurgy and Medicine in rolls.

entries.title: Station of Spiritual Nourishment
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of the Body
entries.summary: Initiates stop aging and need not eat, drink or sleep in suitable auras, but gain Warping and must meditate daily; the effect fails in some realms and auras.
quotes: Characters Initiated into this station gain a Warping Point each year, but do not age.
They must engage in elaborate, delightful labyrinth meditations that take six hours every day, but do not sleep.

entries.title: Station of Perfect Economy of Movement
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of the Body
entries.summary: Once a day after a labyrinth meditation the magus automatically succeeds at one Dexterity-related Ability roll up to a given Ease Factor; the Pious Flaw replaces the Vow.
quotes: the character automatically succeeds on single Dexterity-related Ability roll with an Ease Factor of 21 or less

entries.title: Station of the Microcosm
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of the Body
entries.summary: The magus may cast spells as if holding an Arcane Connection to any mundane place or thing he distinctly recalls, with an Intelligence roll against Ease Factors set by how familiar the place is.
quotes: Places that the magus has visited regularly require a roll against an Ease Factor of 6.
Places the magus visits yearly require rolls against an Ease Factor of 9.
Places the magus visited a long time ago require rolls against an Ease Factor of 12.

entries.title: Threshold of Corporeal Repose
entries.requires: House Criamon: Path of the Body
entries.summary: Final station of the Path of the Body; the magus drinks representations of the four humors from legendary sites and gains a body purified of frailty that no longer ages.
quotes: The magus regains any attributes lost to aging and no longer uses the Aging Point system.

entries.title: Becoming a Quaesitor
entries.summary: How a magus of any House is selected, mentored and appointed as a Quaesitor, and which Abilities the training and exposure covers in game terms.
quotes: In game terms this gives the candidate training and exposure to, Code of Hermes, Hermes Lore, Awareness, Folk Ken and Intrigue.

entries.title: Quaesitor in Good Standing
entries.summary: A Quaesitor needs a current signed letter from the Guernicus Primus to have authority to demand cooperation or preside at Tribunal.
quotes: This letter must be less than seven years old to be valid.

entries.title: Investigation Duties
entries.summary: A Quaesitor must investigate serious complaints but is entitled to seasons of his own each year, which may be accrued.
quotes: He is also entitled to at least three seasons every year to pursue his own studies or attend to covenant responsibilities.

entries.title: Investigation Immunity
entries.requires: Quaesitor (or an agent) in a justified investigation
entries.summary: Limits on when a Quaesitor may use Intellego magic in investigations without breaching the scrying prohibition, what liability remains for incidental discoveries, and who else the immunity covers.
quotes: However, Intellego Mentem magic can never be used on magi or their servants without their permission.

related.text: Scrying on Members of the Order

entries.title: Sanctum Invasions
entries.summary: A Quaesitor may enter a sanctum under investigation, during which time they are under forfeit immunity, though investigation immunity protects them from charges about the invasion.
quotes: While within the sanctum, the Quaesitor and any of their agents are under forfeit immunity.

entries.title: Compensation for Quaesitors
entries.summary: How vis spent on an investigation and a seasonal rate are repaid from Tribunal coffers or by an unfounded complainant, and the share of fines for a Quaesitor who also prosecutes.
quotes: Three pawns per season is a typical figure, but this will vary between sagas and Tribunals.

entries.title: Colentes Arcanorum
entries.summary: The five-member Bonisagus council, chosen at random from magi of cannophori rank or higher, that collects submitted Lab Texts and tractatus and compiles them into folios. Includes the chance that a character is selected and the council's powers over the Primus.
quotes: a player character who has achieved the rank of cannophori has a 1 in 5 chance of being selected

entries.title: Submitted Texts (Colentes)
entries.summary: How many Lab Texts and tractatus a Colens receives during a term, what they look for, and how long it takes to judge a submission.
quotes: It takes a day for Colens Arcanorum to briefly scan a submitted text and determine its value.

entries.title: Tenentes Occultorum
entries.requires: House Bonisagus (magi Trianomae); Minor Status Virtue: Tenens Occultorum
entries.summary: The four seasonal Trianomae officers who guard House secrets and watch mundane seekers of arcane lore, each responsible for a set of Tribunals. Explains how a character can begin play as a Tenens.

related.text: Ars Magica 5th Edition p.32 After Apprenticeship

entries.title: Colloquium Delectorum
entries.summary: The seven-yearly meeting at which the Colentes and Tenentes compile their findings, choose research for the next folio, and can be petitioned about the Primus's orders.

entries.title: The Primus of House Bonisagus
